ai.description: The Green Cascade Frog (Ranidae) reaches 5–8 cm. It is bright green above with dark, irregular spotting and a white belly. Distinctive features include a pointed snout and enlarged, adhesive toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Odorrana livida* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad, white or cream-colored glandular fold running along the upper lip, contrasting with its dark head.
ai.habitat: *Odorrana livida* inhabits fast-flowing, rocky streams within dense evergreen or subtropical hill forests, typically at elevations ranging from 500 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Green Cascade Frog is primarily nocturnal, often perching on mossy rocks near fast-flowing streams to ambush passing insects under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Odorrana livida* is an oviparous breeder that deposits eggs in streams. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season (typically June to August), with clutches laid on rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Odorrana livida* is found in Northeast India, specifically in states like Meghalaya and Nagaland, inhabiting hill streams at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Green Cascade Frog produces a series of high-pitched, bird-like chirps or whistles, typically heard near the fast-flowing, rocky streams of its mountain habitat.
